title: Northland 6 at 6:30: "Staff Say 'Hack'"

fields.headline: LAKEMONT HOSPITAL ON PAPER AFTER OUTAGE
fields.lowerThird: Overnight computer outage; staff say 'hack.' Hospital did not respond before air time on ransomware question
fields.ticker: Lakemont Community Hospital did not respond before air time to questions about whether a cyberattack is to blame • Northland 6 has asked whether patient records were exposed and whether the Lakemont emergency room is open • More on this story in our 7:00 update • Wind chill advisory: feels like -40° across the Twin Ports until 10 a.m. • Glazed roads: use caution on Highway 61 and Highway 53 this morning
fields.anchorBrief: Morning news anchor at a bright TV studio desk with a over-the-shoulder graphic showing a darkened brick community hospital exterior at night in deep winter, snowbanks, frost on the windows, broadcast still frame

instructorNote: Pressure inject: put the still on the main screen. At 06:31, read the follow-up call from the Northland 6 morning producer at 218-555-0158: "We've got a 7:00 update. Can you tell me on the record whether it was a cyberattack, whether patient records were exposed, and whether the ER is open? If not, we'll say you declined again." At 06:33, say that the Duluth Hillside Neighbors group has shared the screenshot with "TOLD you. Hacked." and 44 reactions in 3 minutes. Watch for the PIO to turn the PSEC's 06:15 determination into an on-the-record holding statement of under 150 words. It should cover what is known, what is not yet known and what is being done, and give the next update time. The IC should clear it before it goes out. It should then go to unit managers for bedside use and be posted as a reply in the group. The PIO should also ask Northland 6 to correct the 'hack' framing.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Press photograph, level horizon, 35 mm lens, sharp, natural daylight color. Exterior of a three-story red-brick community hospital before dawn in deep Minnesota winter, shot from across a snow-covered parking lot. Tall plowed snowbanks line the drive, frost crusts the lower windows, and steam rises from rooftop vents into the frigid air. Several upper-floor windows are , and a canopy over the emergency entrance is lit by sodium-vapour lamps. A lone figure in a parka walks toward the entrance with breath fogging. Blue-black pre-dawn sky, light blowing snow, icy glazed pavement reflecting the lamps. Wire-service press photo, 35 mm lens, level framing, sharp detail, cold, tense, quiet mood. Setting: a hospital ambulance bay: two ambulances with doors open, sliding glass doors, paramedics with a stretcher, overcast daylight
